purpose: Establish whether real, public watermark-research evaluation pipelines load encoded images through EXIF-ignoring decode paths, by code inspection of official repositories at recorded commits.
method: For each repository: (1) located the image-loading code used by detection/evaluation entry points via the GitHub git-trees API; (2) fetched raw file content from raw.githubusercontent.com and verified every quoted line against a shallow git clone whose HEAD SHA matches the GitHub commits API; (3) recorded whether the loader honours EXIF orientation (e.g. PIL ImageOps.exif_transpose) or ignores it; (4) grepped every .py/.ipynb/.md file in each clone for 'exif' to test for any orientation handling anywhere in the repository. This is code inspection, not execution: no pipeline was run, and no detection accuracy was measured.

background_facts.PIL.Image.open: Returns pixel data in stored raster order; EXIF orientation is not applied unless ImageOps.exif_transpose (or equivalent) is called explicitly.
background_facts.cv2.imread: OpenCV's default cv2.imread applies the EXIF orientation tag (the study's loader experiment measured 24/24); the tag is ignored only under the explicit IMREAD_IGNORE_ORIENTATION flag.
background_facts.torchvision.datasets.ImageFolder: Default loader is pil_loader: Image.open(...).convert('RGB'); no EXIF transpose.
background_facts.PIL save: PIL's Image.save writes no EXIF orientation tag unless an exif argument is supplied, so JPEGs produced inside these pipelines by PIL do not carry orientation tags.

The paper has been withdrawn by the author and no code or GitHub URL appears in the abstract or comments; no repository was found via GitHub search.

summary.key_finding: Six of the seven inspected repositories that read still images load them through EXIF-ignoring paths (PIL Image.open without exif_transpose, or torchvision's ImageFolder pil_loader); no repository calls exif_transpose or performs other read-side orientation handling. The seventh, invisible-watermark's documented decode example, uses cv2.imread, whose default honours the EXIF tag. (Corrected 2026-09-28 from an initial 7-of-7 count that misclassified cv2.imread; see notes.)
summary.caveat: This is code inspection of eight repositories at the recorded commits, not execution of the pipelines. Loader-census counts include vendored third-party code (e.g. LDM, LPIPS, BSRGAN utilities), and several JPEG re-decode paths within the pipelines consume files written by PIL itself, which carry no orientation tag; the claim is about the decode paths, not about measured detection outcomes.

notes: 2026-09-28 correction: invisible-watermark's documented decode uses cv2.imread, whose default HONOURS EXIF orientation (paper Section 6.2 measured 24/24). The still-image EXIF-ignoring count is therefore 6 of 7, not 7 of 7. Quote evidence unchanged; classification field corrected above.
